selection: 50 existing ingredient pages, selected for frequent Corpus use and useful form/product distinctions. Broad ambiguous labels deferred; not an alphabetical selection.

pages.reason: Frequent seasoning with broad variety scope.
information: A pepper used for pungency as well as flavour. Chillies vary in shape, colour and heat; the general name does not identify one variety.

Keep fresh, dried and chopped instructions attached to the ingredient. A count of peppers does not guarantee a fixed heat level, and a red colour alone does not establish strength. Choose the variety named by the recipe when one is given.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed variety, heat rating or fresh-to-dried ratio.

pages.reason: Frequent herb with leaf/seed distinction.
information: An aromatic herb whose feathery foliage and seeds have separate culinary uses. Dill leaves can be used fresh or dried, while dill seed supplies a different form of seasoning.

Check which part the recipe requests before measuring. A leafy garnish is not the same preparation as a spoonful of seed. Preserve fresh or dried qualifiers rather than assuming equal volumes give equivalent flavour, and remove any unwanted coarse stems when preparing leaves.
pages.uncertainties: No leaf-to-seed or fresh-to-dried equivalence.

pages.reason: Frequent cut; clarify bone and thickness variation.
information: A portion cut from the loin area of a pig. Chops include different named cuts and may be sold with or without bone; their shape and thickness are not uniform.

Choose the cut and preparation specified by the recipe. A thin boneless chop and a thick bone-in portion need different handling even though both are pork chops. The name supplies neither a universal portion weight nor a cooking time.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed thickness, weight or cooking schedule.

pages.reason: Common dried fruit with moisture and colour variants.
information: Dried grapes used for concentrated fruit sweetness and a chewy texture in baking and savoury dishes. Natural and golden raisins are processed differently, and products can also differ in softness.

Match the form to the recipe: whole raisins contribute pieces rather than a dissolved sweetener. If a recipe calls for soaking, treat that as a preparation step rather than an intrinsic property of every raisin. Check the product label when added ingredients matter.
pages.uncertainties: No uniform moisture, preservative or soaking requirement.

pages.reason: Frequent ingredient needing kernel/form context.
information: Corn used as a vegetable commonly means sweetcorn kernels, either on the cob or removed. Sweet corn differs from corn grown for popping or other grain uses.

Read preparation qualifiers such as frozen, defrosted or cooked before using the recipe amount. Whole cobs and loose kernels are different measured forms. This broad entry does not turn cornmeal, popcorn or another processed corn product into an interchangeable replacement for vegetable kernels.
pages.uncertainties: Sweetcorn use explained without narrowing the existing generic identity.

pages.reason: Common broad meat name; cut determines method.
information: Meat from a pig, available as cuts with very different proportions of lean meat, fat, bone and connective tissue. Belly, shoulder, loin and tenderloin are examples rather than interchangeable portions.

Use the recipe’s cut description alongside the general ingredient name. A method intended for one cut should not be transferred solely because another is also pork. Cured or smoked products require their own qualifiers; plain pork does not automatically mean bacon or ham.
pages.uncertainties: No universal cut, preparation state or cooking method.

pages.reason: Frequent produce; separate colour from hot-pepper identity.
information: A red, fleshy bell pepper with thick walls, used raw or cooked. Bell peppers are one form of sweet pepper; red examples generally taste sweeter than green ones.

Remove the stem and prepare the flesh, seeds and inner sections as the recipe directs. Slices, diced pieces and roasted flesh provide different textures. Red bell pepper is not a synonym for a small hot red chilli, even though both ingredients can be red.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed sweetness or equivalence with red chilli.

pages.reason: Common aromatic spice with distinctive whole form.
information: A star-shaped spice fruit with a pronounced anise-like aroma. It is used to perfume broths and other savoury preparations as well as sweet dishes.

Whole pieces flavour a liquid differently from ground spice distributed through a mixture. Keep the recipe’s form and removal instructions in view, rather than treating the hard whole fruit as a soft ingredient. The similar aroma does not make star anise the same ingredient as anise seed.

sources.title: About Star Anise: Uses, Pairings and Recipes

pages.uncertainties: No botanical alias or whole-to-ground conversion.

pages.reason: Frequent blend; avoid fixed formulation.
information: An aromatic spice mixture used to season dishes, rather than a single spice. The cited blend includes spices such as coriander, cumin, cinnamon and cardamom, illustrating its layered character.

Blends vary, so the ingredient name does not specify one universal recipe or heat level. Follow the dish’s instructions for when to add it. Garam masala and curry powder can share ingredients without being the same blend or an automatic spoon-for-spoon replacement.
pages.uncertainties: Product example only; no universal blend composition.

pages.reason: Common vegetable; distinguish edible pods from dried beans.
information: Beans harvested while their pods are tender and eaten as a vegetable. The whole pod is the useful culinary form, unlike mature shelled beans prepared as a dried pulse.

Trim the stem ends and cut or leave the beans whole according to the dish. Preparation changes their size and texture, but does not make them equivalent to cooked kidney beans. Use the recipe’s desired tenderness and product instructions rather than a single cooking time for every bean.
pages.uncertainties: No maturity equivalence or universal cooking time.

pages.reason: Fine sugar form has functional importance.
information: Sugar ground to a fine powder for icings and other smooth sweet preparations. Commercial products may include an anti-caking ingredient such as starch.

Its fine texture is different from ordinary granulated sugar, so changing the form can affect the finished texture. Check the actual product when starch or other ingredients matter. The name does not establish one universal starch content, and a volume of powdered sugar is not automatically an equal mass of granulated sugar.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed starch percentage or volume conversion.

pages.reason: Common allium; clarify colour is not preparation.
information: A bulb onion identified by its white form, used as a chopped or sliced ingredient in raw and cooked dishes. It contributes onion flavour and bulk rather than merely a dry seasoning.

Follow the recipe’s cut size and cooking instructions: finely chopped onion behaves differently from large wedges. The colour name does not imply that it is peeled, cooked or the same size as every other onion. Choose the requested form rather than substituting onion powder by appearance or volume.
pages.uncertainties: No uniform size or pungency claim.

pages.reason: Frequent acidic ingredient; distinguish juice and flavourings.
information: The liquid juice of lime, used to bring citrus flavour and acidity to dishes. Bottled versions may be reconstituted from concentrate; the cited product is one example.

Juice is a different ingredient from grated peel or sweetened lime drinks. Check the recipe and label before measuring, since a lime-flavoured product need not be plain juice. The number of fresh fruits needed is variable, so a measured juice amount should not imply one fixed fruit yield.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed yield, acidity or formulation.

pages.reason: Frequent rich cut; distinguish fresh meat from cured product.
information: A fatty cut from the underside of a pig, with layers of meat and fat. It can be prepared by methods such as roasting or braising, depending on the dish.

Fresh belly is not automatically bacon: curing and other processing change the ingredient. Match rind, bone and portion instructions to the actual cut. Richness and thickness affect the result, so a named cut alone does not provide a reliable cooking time or tell you whether it has already been processed.
pages.uncertainties: No automatic bacon equivalence or preparation-state assumption.

pages.reason: Common label with concentration ambiguity.
information: A prepared tomato ingredient whose concentration needs checking. The cited UK product is a thick, double-concentrated puree, illustrating a form used to add tomato flavour and colour in a small quantity.

Do not infer that concentration from the generic name alone. Read the recipe context and product label before replacing a pourable tomato preparation with a thick concentrate. Their contribution to liquid and tomato intensity can differ; this page does not establish a universal puree-to-paste or puree-to-sauce ratio.
pages.uncertainties: Product-specific concentration; regional identity question left unchanged.

pages.reason: Common poultry name with whole/cut distinctions.
information: Poultry sold whole and as separate portions, including products with different bone and skin preparations. A whole bird and a boneless portion are different starting forms even when both are called turkey.

Retain the cut and state qualifiers in the recipe. Instructions for a whole bird do not automatically apply to pieces, ground meat or cooked leftovers. The generic name alone supplies no portion size, doneness assessment or universal cooking schedule; consult the appropriate product and poultry guidance.
pages.uncertainties: No cooking schedule or readiness assumption.

pages.reason: Common thin-cut meat with handling implications.
information: A cutlet of veal, the meat of a young bovine animal. Cutlets are among the tender veal cuts suited to comparatively quick dry-heat preparations.

The actual thickness, coating and preparation still matter. A breaded cutlet and an uncoated piece are not identical starting points, and pounding is a recipe step rather than an implied part of the ingredient name. Use the specified cut and method instead of transferring a time from a larger roast.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed thickness, origin claim or cooking time.

pages.reason: Common seasoning blend needing scope qualification.
information: A mixture of ground spices used to season dishes. Turmeric, coriander and cumin appear in the cited product, but the name describes a blend rather than one plant or a single fixed formula.

Different mixtures can change colour, aroma and heat. Use the requested blend when specified and read the product label when ingredients matter. Curry powder is not a universal replacement for a prepared curry paste or for every separate spice in a recipe.
pages.uncertainties: No universal composition or heat level.

pages.reason: Frequent pulse with consequential preparation-state distinction.
information: A bean used in dishes such as chilli and beans with rice. Prepared red kidney beans contribute substantial pieces and a firm texture; canned examples are already cooked.

Keep dry, cooked and drained qualifiers distinct when following a recipe. A measured amount of prepared beans is not the same starting quantity as dry beans. Dry kidney beans require appropriate preparation and cooking; instructions for a ready-cooked can should not be applied to an uncooked product.
pages.uncertainties: No dry-to-cooked conversion or home cooking safety protocol.

corpusExamples.raw: (kidney beans, source wording: kidney beans or fresh)

pages.reason: Common pasta shape with useful form context.
information: A short tubular pasta; elbow macaroni is a curved example. Its small pieces suit dishes such as macaroni cheese and pasta salads, where sauce can coat and enter the tubes.

Shape, size and surface can vary between products. Follow the actual package and recipe for cooking rather than treating the name as a fixed timing instruction. Macaroni describes the pasta form, not an already prepared cheese sauce or a complete dish.
pages.uncertainties: Elbows are an example, not the only macaroni form.

pages.reason: Common herb; explain distinction from oregano.
information: An aromatic leafy herb. Sweet marjoram has a comparatively mild, sweet character within the oregano family; that flavour description does not mean that sugar has been added.

The leaves can be dried, but the recipe’s fresh or dried form still matters. Similarity to oregano is useful flavour context, not proof that all oregano and marjoram products are identical. Preserve the named herb and preparation rather than imposing a universal substitution ratio.
pages.uncertainties: No new alias or fixed substitution ratio.

pages.reason: Common cooking liquid; distinguish body and seasoning.
information: A beef-based cooking liquid used to build savoury flavour in sauces and other dishes. Stock commonly emphasises bones and body, although everyday usage overlaps with broth.

Check whether the ingredient is ready to use or concentrated, and whether it is salted. Those details affect a dish more directly than the name alone. A stock label does not guarantee a particular strength or make the liquid equivalent to undiluted beef bouillon.

sources.title: Broth vs. Stock vs. Bone Broth

pages.uncertainties: Practical stock/broth comparison, not a strict new identity boundary.

pages.reason: Common prepared ingredient with texture variation.
information: A peanut-based spread used on its own and in cooking or baking. A smooth product contributes peanut flavour without the larger pieces associated with a chunky preparation.

Formulations can include sweeteners, salt and added fats, so check the actual product when flavour or texture matters. Smoothness is not a guarantee of one ingredient list. A recipe calling for peanut butter does not automatically mean whole peanuts or a differently sweetened peanut sauce.
pages.uncertainties: Manufacturer example only; no universal formulation or dietary claim.

pages.reason: Common meat needing age/cut qualification.
information: A fine-textured meat used in a range of preparations. Younger and more mature rabbits differ in tenderness, so the ingredient name alone does not establish the best cooking method.

Mature rabbit is commonly suited to moist cooking such as braising or stewing. Keep the cut and preparation specified by the recipe rather than assuming every portion cooks like a tender piece of young rabbit. This context does not provide a fixed time or an automatic substitution for chicken.
pages.uncertainties: No age guarantee, cooking schedule or chicken equivalence.

pages.reason: Useful colour qualifier without false heat precision.
information: A red chilli pepper used for pepper flavour and heat. Red identifies its colour, not one particular variety or a guaranteed strength.

Retain any variety and fresh or dried qualifiers when shopping and preparing it. A large mild pepper and a small pungent chilli need not contribute comparable heat. This entry does not equate red chilli with red bell pepper or prescribe a fixed substitution.
pages.uncertainties: No colour-to-heat inference or identity merge.

pages.reason: Common aromatic ingredient with product-strength variation.
information: A culinary rose-scented liquid used to flavour sweet preparations and drinks. It contributes floral aroma rather than the bulk sweetness supplied by sugar.

Use a food product and the amount specified for the particular preparation. Products sold as rose water can differ in formulation and strength; the cited flavouring includes ingredients beyond water. Do not assume that every bottle is alcohol-free, equally concentrated or interchangeable with another rose extract at the same volume.
pages.uncertainties: Product formulation is qualified; no claim that all rose water is identical.

pages.reason: Common noodle family with product-state differences.
information: Noodles made with egg as part of the dough. The cited wheat-flour product is sold frozen, showing that egg noodles are not necessarily a dry pantry ingredient.

Check whether the recipe expects fresh, frozen or dried noodles and follow the actual product’s preparation. Thickness and starting state affect handling. The name does not guarantee a single shape, cooking time or egg proportion, and should not be read as a ready-made noodle dish.
pages.uncertainties: Frozen manufacturer example does not define the whole category.

pages.reason: Common vegetable; distinguish green form and preparation.
information: A green bell pepper with thick, fleshy walls, useful raw or cooked. Green peppers generally have a less sweet character than red and other coloured sweet peppers.

Cut the flesh to suit the dish after preparing the stem and seeds. Strips for a raw salad and pieces for roasting offer different textures. The green colour identifies this requested form; it does not mean every green pepper is a bell pepper or a mild substitute for a green chilli.
pages.uncertainties: No universal sweetness or green-chilli equivalence.

pages.reason: Common broad condiment with formulation variability.
information: A prepared sauce used to add chilli heat and seasoning. The cited red sauce combines peppers, vinegar and salt, illustrating one acidic style within a wider category.

Check the actual sauce before choosing an amount: thickness, sweetness, acidity and heat are not fixed by the generic name. A sauce can bring liquid and seasoning as well as chilli. It is therefore not automatically equivalent to chilli powder or another hot sauce at the same volume.
pages.uncertainties: One product illustrates the category; no universal heat rating.

pages.reason: Named chilli with useful variety distinction.
information: A named type of chilli pepper used for its flesh and pungency. It is more specific than the general word chilli, but individual peppers can still vary.

Use the preparation requested by the recipe. Whole and chopped peppers distribute differently through a dish. A named variety does not establish a guaranteed heat level or an equal-strength replacement for every other chilli.
pages.uncertainties: No guaranteed heat or automatic processing state.

pages.reason: Common prepared dough; explain handling and formulation.
information: A pastry dough built around flour and fat, moistened to bring it together for a crust. The fat and mixing method help determine the finished texture.

Work with the recipe’s specified dough and avoid treating it as puff pastry. Sweet and unsweetened preparations need not suit the same filling. The cited pie-crust guide illustrates fat incorporation and handling; its particular fat mixture and quantities are not a universal formula for every shortcrust pastry.
pages.uncertainties: Pie-crust example supports handling; no mandatory fat or sugar formula.

pages.reason: Common sweetener with crystal-size distinction.
information: A refined sugar used to sweeten foods and contribute to baking structure. Granulated white sugar is a familiar form, but crystal size is an important distinction between sugar products.

Read finer specifications such as caster or powdered sugar when a recipe supplies them. A white appearance does not mean all sugar forms behave identically in mixing or finishing. Brown sugar also contributes molasses character, so changing between the two is more than a colour choice.
pages.uncertainties: No crystal-size equivalence or substitution rule.

pages.reason: Concentrated product requires dilution context.
information: A beef-flavoured preparation used to build savoury cooking liquids and season dishes. The cited roasted beef base is a concentrated paste, rather than a ready-to-use bowl of broth.

Check the supplied form and dilution instructions before measuring. A spoonful of concentrate brings a different strength and seasoning load from the same volume of prepared liquid. The generic name does not establish one concentration or make every bouillon product equivalent to this particular paste.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed dilution ratio or universal product form.

pages.reason: Common spice; distinguish pod, seed and variety.
information: An aromatic spice whose seeds are used in cooking, either within pods or removed and ground. Green cardamom and larger dark cardamom types are distinct forms, not simply different package sizes.

Keep the variety and whole or ground instruction with the recipe amount. Pods and loose seeds do not occupy equal volumes or disperse flavour in the same way. This broad entry does not establish that black and green cardamom can always replace one another unchanged.
pages.uncertainties: No variety merge or whole-to-ground conversion.

pages.reason: Coarse seasoning needs heat qualification.
information: Dried chilli broken into small pieces, often with visible seeds. The coarse texture gives a different distribution through a dish from a finely ground pepper powder.

Use the requested flakes and intended heat level as context, since products vary in pepper variety and strength. The name does not guarantee one fixed heat rating or make flakes equivalent to a mild red paprika. Follow the recipe amount without assuming every jar has identical potency.

sources.title: About Red Pepper Uses, Pairings and Recipes

pages.uncertainties: No new alias or universal heat rating.

pages.reason: Common flavour ingredient with brewed/solid ambiguity.
information: Coffee begins with seeds from coffee fruit that are processed and roasted. Ground roasted coffee is used to prepare a drink, so the brewed liquid and the grounds are different ingredient forms.

Read the recipe’s preparation before measuring coffee. An amount of brewed coffee supplies liquid as well as flavour; the same amount of dry grounds does not. The general name alone cannot establish concentration or justify replacing a liquid with a solid coffee product.
pages.uncertainties: No assumed brewed state, strength or conversion.

pages.reason: Seed spice should remain distinct from bulb vegetable.
information: An aromatic seed seasoning with an anise-like character, used in preparations including sausages, fish dishes and soups. It is a different culinary part from the swollen bulb of Florence fennel.

Whole seeds supply small pieces as well as flavour, while grinding changes how they distribute. Follow the form named in the recipe rather than substituting a bulb measure or another anise-scented spice automatically. Similar aroma does not establish equal strength or an identical ingredient.
pages.uncertainties: No seed/bulb or anise substitution ratio.

pages.reason: Compound sauce needs flavour/formulation context.
information: A sweet, savoury sauce commonly used in marinades, stir-fries and as a dip. The cited product combines a soybean-based preparation with sweeteners and seasonings.

It contributes more than salt, so it is not simply another name for soy sauce. Check the actual label when ingredients matter; formulations can include wheat or other components. Use its texture and sweetness deliberately rather than assuming any dark sauce will produce the same result.
pages.uncertainties: Product example; no universal allergen or dietary claim.

pages.reason: Fat product with important formulation variation.
information: A manufactured fat product used for spreading and, in suitable formulations, cooking or baking. It differs from dairy butter in composition, and products sold alongside it can have different proportions of fat and water.

Check that the particular product is appropriate for the recipe. A soft spread and a baking margarine need not behave alike when creamed or heated. The name alone does not guarantee a universal fat percentage or a successful equal-volume replacement for butter.

sources.title: Is It a Butter, Margarine or Spread?

pages.uncertainties: No universal legal fat threshold or baking equivalence.

pages.reason: Cured pork ingredient needs distinction from fresh belly.
information: A cured pork-belly preparation. The cited rolled pancetta is salted, seasoned and aged, giving a prepared ingredient with a different flavour from untreated fresh belly.

Read the product form and the recipe’s slicing or dicing instruction. A rolled piece and prepared small pieces are different starting forms, and seasoning affects the dish as well as the meat itself. This example does not establish a universal spice mixture or make every bacon product equivalent to pancetta.
pages.uncertainties: Rolled example only; no curing recipe or readiness guarantee.

pages.reason: Named cheese with milk and maturity distinctions.
information: A hard sheep’s-milk cheese with a savoury, increasingly sharp character as it matures. Its firm texture makes it useful for grating, while less mature forms can also be used as table cheese.

Choose the form and maturity appropriate to the dish. Grated cheese distributes differently from a solid piece, and its seasoning contribution matters. A shared hard texture does not make Pecorino Romano identical to every other grating cheese or establish a universal replacement ratio.
pages.uncertainties: No automatic Parmesan equivalence or fixed maturity.

pages.reason: Common chilli sauce with distinct seasoning profile.
information: A chilli sauce style combining pepper heat with garlic and sweetness. The cited product uses red jalapeños and other seasonings to make a thick sauce.

Treat that product as an example, not a universal formulation. Sriracha contributes texture and flavour beyond chilli alone, so replacing it with a thin vinegar-led hot sauce may change the dish. Read the actual ingredients and recipe amount rather than assuming all bottles have the same sweetness or strength.
pages.uncertainties: Generic style retained; no brand identity or fixed heat.

pages.reason: Tart spice with salted-product distinction.
information: A tart berry seasoning used to bring a bright, citrus-like character to food. The cited culinary sumac product is chopped and cured with salt.

Check whether the actual product contains added salt before seasoning the rest of the dish. That cured example does not mean every sumac is salted. Its tart flavour is useful context, but it is not a measured replacement for lemon juice and does not supply the same liquid.
pages.uncertainties: Culinary product only; no foraging advice or acidity conversion.

pages.reason: Fish ingredient with whole/fillet preparation distinctions.
information: A fish ingredient sold in forms such as whole dressed fish and fillets. Rainbow trout is one familiar example with relatively mild flesh, but the broad name does not specify every product detail.

Keep skin, bone and portion instructions visible when preparing the dish. A whole fish and a fillet have different shapes and handling needs. The name does not guarantee a particular size, production method or universal cooking time, so use the actual product and recipe context.
pages.uncertainties: Rainbow product is an example, not the entire trout category.

pages.reason: Ground spice form needs colour/flavour context.
information: A yellow ground spice with an earthy flavour, used in rice, vegetables and seasoning mixtures. It contributes its own flavour as well as a strong colour.

The powder is a prepared dry form rather than a fresh piece of turmeric. Keep that distinction when following a recipe: a spoonful of powder and a piece of fresh material are not the same measured ingredient. No automatic conversion or nutritional claim follows from its colour or culinary use.
pages.uncertainties: No fresh-to-ground ratio or health claim.

pages.reason: Pepper form differs in processing and appearance.
information: A pepper spice made from ripe pepper berries with the outer covering removed, then dried. Ground white pepper supplies pepper flavour while remaining less visually conspicuous in pale sauces and soups.

Choose the specified whole or ground form. Its pale appearance does not mean it is a neutral powder, and should not be used as a measure of strength. The comparison with black pepper explains appearance and processing without establishing a universal equal-strength substitution.
pages.uncertainties: No fixed pungency or black-pepper substitution ratio.

pages.reason: Common savoury liquid; qualify stock overlap.
information: A beef-based liquid used to add flavour and moisture to soups, rice and other dishes. Broth commonly involves meat and aromatics simmered in water, though recipes and packaged formulations vary.

Check salt and concentration before using it as the main liquid. Stock and broth overlap in everyday naming, so the label alone does not guarantee a lighter or stronger product. Prepared broth is not automatically interchangeable with undiluted bouillon at the same volume.

sources.title: Broth vs. Stock vs. Bone Broth

pages.uncertainties: No strict stock/broth identity rule or concentration guarantee.

pages.reason: Common broad ingredient with part/form ambiguity.
information: Coconut provides edible flesh as well as water, and is processed into several different food products. The flesh is a different starting ingredient from the liquid naturally inside the fruit.

Use the part and preparation specified by the recipe. Grated or dried flesh, coconut milk and coconut water do not contribute the same texture or amount of liquid. This general entry supplies that distinction without silently choosing a particular processed product whenever a recipe says coconut.
pages.uncertainties: No part mapping, desiccation yield or milk substitution.

pages.reason: Useful cheese example in current curry recipes.
information: A fresh dairy cheese supplied in forms such as a block that can be cut into pieces. The cited product uses milk solids and an acid ingredient in its preparation.

Match the cut size and handling to the recipe; cubes are a preparation of the cheese rather than a different ingredient. Check the actual product for composition and storage instructions. This example does not make every fresh cheese interchangeable with paneer or prescribe a home cheesemaking method.
pages.uncertainties: No universal milk composition, melting rule or production method.

pages.reason: Common broad meat name with cut-dependent handling.
information: Meat from young sheep, sold in cuts including shoulder, rack, loin and leg. These portions differ in structure, so lamb is not a single uniform piece of meat.

Read the cut and preparation along with the name before choosing a method. A dish written for a shoulder does not automatically supply suitable instructions for a small loin portion. Older sheep meat is commonly termed mutton; this distinction does not create a fixed size or cooking schedule for lamb.
pages.uncertainties: No universal cut, age test or cooking schedule.
